question.text: Given EUR/USD = 1.1125/1.1150 and USD/INR = 75.64/75.65, what is the bid rate for EUR/INR?

explanation.text: The Logic: To SELL EUR (bid side), a customer: (1) Sells EUR at the bid rate of 1.1125 USD, and (2) Sells the USD received at the bid rate of 75.64 INR. Therefore, EUR/INR bid = 1.1125 × 75.64 = 84.1495. The corresponding offer side is 1.1150 × 75.65 = 84.3498. The Trap: Mixing bid and offer rates across the two legs gives an incorrect result. Note: Source: NISM Series I (Currency Derivatives) workbook, pp.29-30 — for EURINR / GBPINR style cross rates the bid (offer) is derived by multiplying the bid (offer) rates of the underlying pairs. Other cross rates such as JPYINR are derived through division, so the multiply-both-sides rule is specific to this family of cross rates.
